source.stem: What always increases during the development of an organism?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Lukewarm milk turns into curd immediately when the starter is mixed in.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Only the cold bowl forms curd; the lukewarm bowl stays liquid because warmth inhibits the starter.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Milk kept boiling hot after adding the starter will form curd just as lukewarm milk does.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Both bowls have formed curd because both taste sour.

intelligence.enrichment: When a small spoonful of curd is mixed into lukewarm milk and left for a few hours, the milk turns into curd and becomes a little sour. Cold milk with the same curd starter does not curdle in the same way, although it may become a little sour. Curd starter plus lukewarm milk and time -> curd formation; curd starter plus cold milk -> little or no curdling. The learner correctly applies this rule: When a small spoonful of curd is mixed into lukewarm milk and left for a few hours, the milk turns into curd and becomes a little sour. Cold milk with the same curd starter does not curdle in the same way, although it may become a little sour. Any milk with a spoonful of curd will become curd equally fast, whether it is cold or lukewarm.
